newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch favour swift EU entry for East Europeans.
newsitem.headline: Dutch favour swift EU entry for East Europeans.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister and current European Union president Wim Kok urged EU members on Thursday to speed up the process of enlarging the union.
Addressing reporters after talks with visiting Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn, Kok said negotiations on the admission of new members would start in early 1998.
Kok declined to say how long the admission process would take but he said the Netherlands wanted to see the creation of an "undivided Europe" through the enlargement of the EU.
The entry of Central and Eastern European countries like Hungary symbolised that process, he said.
"We want to speed up that process as much as possible without forgetting the quality," Kok said.
Other issues discussed by the two leaders included the possibility of the Netherlands and Hungary cooperating in the fight against organised crime.
